core_obligations: Deduce that localisations at maximal ideals are discrete valuation rings (proof lines 10889-10891).
Conclude that the target is a Noetherian normal ring of dimension one (proof lines 10892-10893).
Apply the structure theorem to write it as a finite product of normal domains of dimension one (proof lines 10893-10895).
Identify those factors as Dedekind domains (proof lines 10896-10898).
proof_roadmap: Local rings are discrete valuation rings (proof lines 10889-10891).
Noetherian normal of dimension one (proof lines 10892-10893).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an etale ring map with Dedekind domain source has a target which is a finite product of Dedekind domains, and in particular has discrete valuation rings as localisations at maximal ideals. The proof first identifies the localisations at maximal ideals as discrete valuation rings, combining the preservation of dimension and regularity along etale maps with the characterisation of discrete valuation rings. It then follows that the target is a Noetherian normal ring of dimension one, and the structure theorem for such rings identifies it as a finite product of normal domains of dimension one, which are Dedekind domains.
